source.description:
## Context

Sessions you live in should float up below the attention-ranked head. Pure alphabetical sorts bury them.

## What to build

- On switch (`jump_to_target`), record `session_id` + timestamp to `~/.local/state/xtmux/frecency`.
- Compute a frecency score (recent + frequency) and use it to break ties below attention rank.
- Compact the log periodically (cap N entries).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Frequently/recently switched sessions rank higher among non-attention rows.
- [ ] Log file bounded (no unbounded growth).
- [ ] Degrades gracefully if state dir unwritable.
- [ ] Contract tests pass (sort change).

## Approach notes

- Score: recency-decayed count (e.g. last 100 switches, weight by age).
- Keep the attention-ranked head untouched (WAIT/RUN first), frecency only orders the rest.
- Layer: core (score) + boundary (state file). Depends-on: t0.
source.title: Frecency: persist last-used + count for idle-tail ranking
